headline: Decomposition and foundation-model methods resolve state-specific programs across aging, cancer and cell types
label: Modular Decomposition Of Disease States
summary: New methods decompose omics into pathway, module, flux and state-level programs, extending disease modeling beyond single-gene or bulk comparisons.
synthesis: The common thread is replacing gene-level or bulk comparisons with structured, interpretable units of variation that can be linked to disease or aging. Tensor decomposition (HOSVD) selects aging genes across mouse hippocampus and colon; PathwayTheme decomposes pathway scores; robust ICA yields 105 iModulons in 778 CHO samples. Metabolic work (Recon3D modeling across 33 TCGA types; M-SCAN flux inference from RNA, mutations and kcat) moves to sample-specific flux. Single-cell items operate at state level: UCE-based mapping of 22,161 bridges among 614 states, a review of 161 cell-cell communication methods, and the LACA cross-species aging resource covering 134 species. What is new is the breadth of units (modules, fluxes, state transitions), though the items do not share one integrated pipeline or consistently resolve cell types.
